Routing notes:
- Do not choose option C by default. It was rejected for REQ-2401 through REQ-2408 and REQ-2410.
- Option C was accepted only once (REQ-2409: large refund, east region, Finance Desk, repeat follow-up), so this may reflect a specific exception or malformed/truncated option text rather than a general rule.
- Available standard choices are A (standard queue) and B (priority desk); prefer evaluating these unless there is clear evidence that C is valid.
- Request attributes include type (refund/claim/shipment), size, region, sender department, and message cues (repeat request, bounced form, regional-office origin, scanned paperwork). No reliable mapping from these attributes to A/B has yet been established.
- Treat truncated option lists cautiously; do not infer that a missing or partial C description makes C valid.

Routing notes:
- Do not choose C by default. It was rejected for REQ-2401–2408, REQ-2410, and all recent cases REQ-2411–2418. C was accepted only once (REQ-2409: large refund, east region, Finance Desk, repeat follow-up), likely a specific exception or malformed/truncated option list.
- Standard choices are usually A (standard queue) and B (priority desk). Evaluate A/B first; treat truncated or partial C text cautiously. Do not infer validity from missing option descriptions.
- Recent validated outcomes:
  - B: REQ-2411 (large invoice, north, no-rush/confirm receipt); REQ-2416 (large shipment, south, no-rush/confirm receipt); REQ-2417 (small shipment, east, repeat-like wording).
  - A: REQ-2412 (large shipment, north, bounced form); REQ-2413 (large claim, east, regional office); REQ-2414 (large invoice, east, repeat request); REQ-2415 (large claim, east, regional office); REQ-2419 (small shipment, south, bounced form); REQ-2420 (small claim, north, no-rush/confirm receipt).
- Do not assume “repeat,” “regional office,” size, region, sender department, or request type independently determines A/B: similar cues have produced different choices. Use the combined attribute pattern and these examples, while seeking more evidence.
- REQ-2418 included an apparent extra “D” after C; the option list may be malformed. Its attempted A was rejected, so inspect complete option text when available rather than assuming only A/B/C.

Routing notes:
- Do not choose C by default. It was rejected for REQ-2401–2408, REQ-2410, and REQ-2411–2418, with one acceptance at REQ-2409 (large refund, east, Finance Desk, repeat follow-up). However, newer cases show A/B can also be rejected, so C may be valid when the request pattern or complete option list supports it.

- Do not assume “repeat,” “regional office,” size, region, sender department, request type, urgency, or paperwork format independently determines the route. Similar cues now produce both A and B outcomes.
- Use the combined attribute pattern, but prioritize complete option text and verified outcomes. When A and B are both plausible—or one is rejected—consider that a truncated C or other option may be the intended valid choice.
